title: Micro-CT supports morphological and putative functional transformation of silk glands in Manduca sexta
content:
Abstract
Silk production is a key evolutionary adaptation with important ecological and behavioral roles. In most Lepidoptera, specialized larval silk glands transform into adult salivary glands during metamorphosis. In the Tobacco hornworm, Manduca sexta (Sphingidae), this transformation is even more pronounced. Previous studies suggest that silk production is restricted to first-instar larvae, with subsequent instars no longer producing silk. However, how silk gland morphology and organization change throughout larval development remains poorly understood. Using high-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), we generated the first in situ 3D reconstructions of M. sexta silk glands across first, third, and fifth instars. First-instars displayed a tripartite gland organization with thick epithelia and lumina filled with dense secretory material. In contrast, later instars exhibited enlarged, highly convoluted tubular glands with reduced regional differentiation, thinner epithelia, and largely hollow lumina, suggesting a potential shift in glandular function. We also observed substantial remodeling of the spinneret and spigot in fifth instars, consistent with previous studies. These findings reveal pronouced ontogenic changes in silk gland morphology that may reflect previously proposed functional shifts during development, highlighting the developmental plasticity of this organ.
